description: Claim/lease semantics for work claims. Data only: no lease mechanism exists in mcp/server.py @ d8332e0a - the 'defined' block is the W1 target definition, not a description of enforced behavior.

current.evidence: no claim/lease code path in the TeamHarness MCP; the only TTL constant is MATRIX_ATTACHMENT_CONTEXT_TTL_SECONDS = 30 * 60 (Matrix attachment-context cache, unrelated to work claims)
current.current_write_mutex: per-file atomic replace (same-dir tempfile + fsync + os.replace in _atomic_write_text) plus an in-process per-path threading.Lock for session records (SESSION_WRITE_LOCKS); no cross-process lockfile and no CAS check in the Python write path; the design contract (project-task-runtime-design.md) names single-writer + compare-and-swap (CAS) as the cross-process boundary

defined.renew: renew extends the expiry from the renew time; a renew is idempotent for the same holder + claim identity and never extends more than ttl_seconds from the most recent successful renew; a renew after expiry fails and the claim must be re-acquired
defined.expiry: lazy: there is no background reaper; a claim is treated as expired when an acquire/renew/operate check reads its expiry timestamp in the past, and the next acquire may take the work

rationale.mutex: the design contract already mandates single-writer + CAS for cross-process state changes, so the lease mutex reuses cas (conditional write on the claim record) instead of introducing lockfiles
rationale.ttl_seconds: proposed range around a 300s default: short enough that a dead holder's claim frees within one leader wake-up cycle, long enough to cover a normal working turn; W1 proposal, no code source
